solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: How copper might become coper, without much enthusiasm

definitions.meaning: the heart of 'copper' is its double P; keep only half of that heart and the word shrinks to 'coper'
the ordinary adverb for doing something with little zeal

explanation.surface: A policeman going through the motions, turning up for duty with no real zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: Read HALF-HEARTEDLY literally: the heart of COPPER is PP, and halving it leaves COPER. The second half of the clue is the plain meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing a job without much enthusiasm is doing it half-heartedly, a standard synonym for lacking zeal or commitment.

clue.text: Second Harry Potter book reviewed could offer boost to this London location

indicators.note: to review is to go over again, and here the book title is gone over and rearranged
the jumbled title could hand over the words 'boost to', leaving the location behind as the remainder

parts.note: the whole phrase as printed is the fodder, 21 letters
these two words are taken out of the jumbled fodder

explanation.surface: A reader wondering whether a good review of Chamber of Secrets could lift a London landmark's fortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: A subtractive anagram: the letters of SECOND HARRY POTTER BOOK make HYDE PARK CORNER plus BOOST TO. 'Second Harry Potter book' pulls you towards the title Chamber of Secrets, which plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyde Park Corner is a famous road junction and landmark at the south-east edge of Hyde Park in central London.

clue.text: Handful of gladioli lacking colour

indicators.note: a handful is a small portion taken from a bigger bunch, so only a few letters of the phrase are wanted

parts.note: runs across the end of the flower name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A bunch of gladioli that have faded and lost their colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking' tempts you to remove letters, but it simply supplies the last three letters of the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a pale purple shade named after the flowering shrub, so it is an example of a colour.

clue.text: Chiller to air his rear potentially

indicators.note: the phrase is only potentially the answer, once its letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone needing a cold draught to cool their backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chiller' looks like a fridge or a cold wind, but here it is a scary story or film.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiller is a frightening thriller, and a hair-raiser is likewise a story terrifying enough to make hair stand on end.

clue.text: Shellfish from solitary sailor

explanation.surface: A lone seafarer catching and eating shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads in reverse clue order: the sailor comes first, then the solitude.
explanation.definitionFit: An abalone is an edible sea snail with an ear-shaped shell lined with mother-of-pearl, a kind of shellfish.

clue.text: A point or taunt possibly

indicators.note: the words could possibly be something else once their letters are shifted around

explanation.surface: Debating tactics: make a proper argument or simply jeer at the opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A point' is the French cookery term à point, cooked just right, not a point in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Food done à point is cooked exactly right, which English describes as cooked to a turn, so the idioms are equivalent.

clue.text: Money owed from French telephone company

parts.note: British Telecom, the UK's main phone company

explanation.surface: An unpaid bill from a French phone provider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' looks like a link word, but 'from French' together means translate 'from' into French.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is a sum that one party owes to another, the literal meaning of money owed.

clue.text: Somewhere for kids to buy lunch that's refurbished, not new

indicators.note: something refurbished has been done over and put back together in a new arrangement
'new' abbreviates to a single letter, and 'not' tells you to leave that letter out of the phrase

parts.note: N = new, removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: A renovated café where children can get their midday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the N out of TO BUY LUNCH and rearrange the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth club is a centre offering leisure activities for young people, so it is a place meant for kids.

clue.text: What Caesar's wife was briefly from the beginning, with European touch

indicators.note: a brief version of a phrase is cut short, so the Latin phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: Latin 'ab ovo', literally from the egg, with its last letter cut
a touch of something is a trace, as in 'a suspicion of garlic'

explanation.surface: A classical riddle about Caesar's wife, told briefly and from the start with a European flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: Julius Caesar divorced his wife Pompeia because 'Caesar's wife must be above suspicion'. 'Touch' in the sense of a faint trace is the hard step.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says Caesar's wife must be beyond any doubt or reproach, so the definition quotes the phrase's origin.

clue.text: Young boy returning to a country in recession with a priest

indicators.note: going back the way it came, so the young boy is written backwards
a recession is a moving back, so the country is written backwards too

parts.note: the article taken as it stands
the final article, taken as it stands

explanation.surface: A boy travelling home to a struggling economy, accompanied by a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In recession' reads like economics but is a second reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama is the chief spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism, a lama being a Buddhist monk or priest.

clue.text: Promotional words blemish book

explanation.surface: Advertising copy that spoils a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The book in the wordplay fits the definition too, since blurbs appear on book covers.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurb is the short piece of praise printed on a jacket to sell something, so it is advertising copy.

clue.text: On reflection, go over to find horse

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front

parts.note: to recap is to go over the main points again

explanation.surface: Thinking a race again after the event to pick out a winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' sounds like 'after thinking it over' but asks for the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacer is a horse bred or trained to move at a pace, the lateral gait used in harness racing.

clue.text: Old star making a comeback is a burden

indicators.note: coming back means going the opposite way, so the star is written backwards

explanation.surface: A faded celebrity attempting a return that becomes a drag for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old star' reads as a has-been celebrity; here the star is the astronomical one.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a duty or responsibility that weighs on someone, which is what a burden means figuratively.

clue.text: Rich and average — words that encompass tasteless person

indicators.note: the two named words enclose the answer between them, straddling where they meet

parts.note: the tail of the first word, its final two letters
the opening two letters of the second word

explanation.surface: A snobbish remark about someone both wealthy and ordinary lacking good taste.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually the hidden run skips 'and': it is RICH plus AVERAGE that holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chav is British slang, often derogatory, for a young person seen as brash and flashily vulgar in dress and manner.

clue.text: Your fiance could become aggressive

indicators.note: the words could turn into something else when their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A warning that a partner may turn nasty after the engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a relationship warning; the fodder is simply the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: In-your-face describes confrontational, blatantly provocative behaviour, close in meaning to pushy or aggressive.

clue.text: Migrate to compose dance music

indicators.note: composing means arranging parts into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician moving abroad to write tunes for dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compose' fits the musical surface, which disguises it as an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtime is a syncopated piano style from around 1900, popular for dances such as the cakewalk.

clue.text: Athletic facility in German school?

definitions.meaning: a hall for sport and exercise
the academic secondary school in Germany

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the German sense, where the same word names a grammar school.
explanation.definitionFit: In English a gymnasium is a sports hall; in Germany a Gymnasium is the selective secondary school preparing pupils for university.

clue.text: Perplexity of deficiency

definitions.meaning: the noun, a state of bewilderment
split cryptically as 'not' plus 'plus': the opposite of a surplus, a minus or shortfall

explanation.walkthrough: The noun sense is old but in dictionaries: to be at a nonplus is to be baffled. The second meaning is cryptic, splitting the word into not plus.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun nonplus means a state of utter bewilderment, and a shortfall is literally a lack of plus.

clue.text: Commanding officer and representative before getting MC

parts.note: a Member of Parliament represents constituents
old or poetic word for before

explanation.surface: An officer and an MP both awaiting the Military Cross.
explanation.walkthrough: MC here is master of ceremonies, not the Military Cross the officer suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A compere hosts a show and introduces the acts, the job of a master of ceremonies.

clue.text: Right in other than passage

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, so the right goes into 'other than'

explanation.surface: A terse note about something correct being anything but a way through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' could be a corridor, but here it is a piece of text.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is an extract taken from a longer text or piece of music, just as a passage is.

clue.text: Diamond found in coach parked by hotel within memory

indicators.note: a vehicle parked by something sits alongside it, so the coach goes next to the rest
the hotel goes inside the memory

parts.note: H = hotel in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A jewel discovered on a bus left outside a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parked by' puts the coach next to the rest; it sits at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is an equal-sided parallelogram, the geometric shape commonly called a diamond.

clue.text: Area supporting full-bodied bean

indicators.note: in a down entry a support sits underneath, so the area goes after the other piece

parts.note: robust means strong and rich in flavour

explanation.surface: A region that grows strong-tasting coffee beans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full-bodied' fits coffee tasting, so the surface cleverly supports the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Robusta is a hardy coffee species and the name for its beans, stronger and more bitter than arabica.

clue.text: Engineers in the morning will be a bore

definitions.note: verb sense, to bore out a hole

parts.note: RE = Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers complaining that the early shift is tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a dull person but is the verb for widening a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: To ream is to enlarge or finish a drilled hole with a reamer, a specialised kind of boring.

clue.text: Crustlike surface of sheath poet abandoned

indicators.note: the poet is abandoned, left out of the sword's sheath

parts.note: a bard is a poet, and is removed

explanation.surface: A poet walking away and leaving a rough crusted sword cover behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The bard is conveniently at the end of the sheath, so removing him leaves the first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is the dry crust forming over a healing wound, and more generally any rough crusty layer.

clue.text: More than one spoke of gods in African music

indicators.note: the gods sit inside the music

explanation.surface: Someone who spoke about deities in African songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' looks like the past tense of speak; it is a wheel spoke.
explanation.definitionFit: The spokes of a wheel run from hub to rim, each one a radius, so several spokes are radii.

clue.text: Soldier leaving poisonous plant for sea captain

indicators.note: the soldier leaves the plant's name and is dropped

parts.note: a poisonous plant of the nightshade family
a man is a private soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier swapping a toxic plant for a naval commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is a link word here, not a swap instruction. Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan English captain who sailed around the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Drake was a famous Elizabethan naval commander and explorer, so he is a celebrated example of a sea captain.

clue.text: A giant that's highly excited

parts.note: Gog, a legendary giant, paired with Magog

explanation.surface: A thrilled giant.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are legendary giants, traditionally guardians of the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly expectant and full of excitement or curiosity, a close synonym for keyed up.

clue.text: No objection to complying with close observation

indicators.note: 'no' means without, so the objection is removed

parts.note: OB, a dictionary abbreviation for objection, is removed

explanation.surface: Someone raising no objection to following rules under scrutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is a link here, not an addition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eying something means looking at it carefully and attentively, the verbal noun for watching closely.

clue.text: Emperor's artist on expedition about beginning of Thebes

indicators.note: the artist is placed on, and so before, the expedition
the expedition goes around the beginning letter of the city

explanation.surface: An emperor's painter on a trip around the ancient city of Thebes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is possessive: Ras Tafari was the Emperor's name before his coronation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ras Tafari Makonnen was the pre-coronation title and name of Haile Selassie, Emperor of Ethiopia.

clue.text: The 'Men Behaving Badly' with name-dropping is one that didn't happen

indicators.note: behaving badly suggests disorder, so the letters are scrambled
the name is dropped, so its single-letter abbreviation is taken out

explanation.surface: A nod to the 1990s British sitcom Men Behaving Badly, about two laddish flatmates.
explanation.walkthrough: The title's last word is the anagram signal, not fodder. Men Behaving Badly was a popular 1990s British sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: A might-have-been is an event or possibility that never came to pass, so it describes what did not occur.
